home.title:
Content operations.
Digital platforms.
home.intro: I'm Livi. I work with teams whose content is hard to find, hard to reuse, or risky to publish. The projects here are the models and workflows I use to get that under control.

about.title: About Livi.
about.lede: Content operations, CMS, DAM and digital platforms.
about.body: I work with editors to map how content moves, then leave a model and a workflow they can run without me.

principles.title: Start with the editors
principles.body: I sit with the people who publish and watch them do a real task before I change anything.

principles.title: Name an owner
principles.body: Every record gets a person who can change it, a reason to exist and a way to retire it.

principles.title: Leave it easy to run
principles.body: The next owner should be able to find the source of truth without calling me.

contact.title: Get in touch.
contact.lede: Open to content operations and digital platform work.
contact.subject: Content & digital platform opportunity

home.title:
DJ sets.
Behind the decks.
home.intro: Livicee is the DJ side of me. Five mixes, from the slow open to the wind-down.

about.title: About Livicee.
about.body: Same person, different collection. I pick for the room first: the hour, who is there, how much space the music needs. Files go on when I have them to share.

principles.title: Read the room
principles.body: The hour and who is there decide the record, not a genre label.

principles.title: Leave room for a turn
principles.body: A set that only plays what people already know gets dull, so I keep a path open for something they didn’t expect.

principles.title: Think in hours
principles.body: Each selection here is a stretch of the night and where it goes next.

projects.json.title: Asset library migration
projects.json.subtitle: Digital asset management
projects.json.summary: A messy shared drive turned into a library editors can search, with ownership and usage kept on each file.

facts.label: Output
facts.value: Metadata model, migration plan, ownership matrix

story.label: Contribution
story.title: How I approach a migration
story.body: I start with a representative slice of the library, not the whole drive. Once we know what people search for, I map the old fields, run a pilot with editors, then move in batches so rights and owners aren’t lost on the way in.

projects.json.title: Reusable content model
projects.json.subtitle: Content architecture
projects.json.summary: A model for content that shows up in more than one place, so editors change it once and the rest of the site stays in step.

story.label: Contribution
story.title: Pulling content out of pages
story.body: I take the parts that get reused (people, topics, assets) out of the page they live on and link them back in as references. I test it with an editing task: can someone update a name or a topic without hunting through six pages?

projects.json.title: Editorial request to release
projects.json.subtitle: Workflow & enablement
projects.json.summary: A publishing path with an owner, one review round, and a clear publish check at the end.

story.label: Contribution
story.title: Where the delay was
story.body: Most of the delay came from requests with no owner. I mapped where requests arrive, cut the states down, put feedback in one place and made the publish check explicit. The contributor guide uses the same words as the workflow, so onboarding isn’t a second system.

projects.json.title: Shared vocabulary
projects.json.subtitle: Taxonomy & governance
projects.json.summary: The names people already use, written down so search, tags and navigation agree.

story.label: Contribution
story.title: Choosing the words and who owns them
story.body: I compare labels, search terms and navigation, pick preferred names and useful synonyms, then name who can change a term. Without an owner, the vocabulary ends up forgotten in a spreadsheet.

projects.json.title: Content inventory & decisions
projects.json.subtitle: Content quality
projects.json.summary: A register that turns a long list of pages into keep, improve, merge or retire, with the reason still on the row.

story.label: Contribution
story.title: Recording the decisions
story.body: Purpose, audience, owner and condition go on the record before I recommend a change. If the evidence is missing, the row says so rather than marking the page as failed. Another editor can read the register and see why something was kept or cut.

projects.json.title: Asset rights & reuse
projects.json.subtitle: Digital asset management
projects.json.summary: Usage rules that travel with the file, so an editor can see whether it is safe to drop into a new piece of work.

story.label: Contribution
story.title: Showing what’s missing
story.body: Permitted use, source, expiry and the responsible contact sit on the asset. If a field is empty, the editor has a next step instead of a guess, and unanswered rights questions stay open until someone owns them.

projects.json.title: CMS authoring experience
projects.json.subtitle: Editorial interfaces
projects.json.summary: A content form ordered around the editor's task, with guidance and checks at the point they type.

story.label: Contribution
story.title: Building the form around the task
story.body: Fields follow the order an editor decides things in. Public copy is kept apart from internal notes, and validation is written in plain language. I test drafting, revising and handing over, not just whether the record saves.

projects.json.title: Publishing readiness
projects.json.subtitle: Release assurance
projects.json.summary: A release check covering the content, its links and the path a visitor takes, as well as whether the build deployed.

story.label: Contribution
story.title: Checking before release
story.body: Linked records, copy approval, media alternatives and contact routes get checked together. Anything still open has an owner and a release decision. A passing build doesn’t tell you whether the site works for a visitor, so someone uses it first.

projects.json.title: Team knowledge handover
projects.json.subtitle: Documentation & enablement
projects.json.summary: Task-based documentation so the next owner can run the content system without a call to the last person who touched it.

story.label: Contribution
story.title: Writing the jobs
story.body: I organise the guidance around the work a new owner has to do: update a record, unblock a review, find the right contact. Each task points to the source of truth, and someone is named to keep it up to date.

projects.json.title: Review & retirement
projects.json.subtitle: Content maintenance
projects.json.summary: A review loop for published content, with a set way to archive it when it has done its job.

story.label: Contribution
story.title: Every record gets a review date
story.body: Every live record gets an owner and a review date. Out of date, duplicated or unused content has a path to archive, and inbound links get checked before anything disappears. The reason stays on the record.

experience.json.title: Content & asset operations
experience.json.subtitle: DAM, vocabulary, rights, lifecycle
experience.json.summary: Keeping libraries searchable, terms agreed, usage visible, and published content on a review cycle.

story.label: Practice
story.title: The day-to-day of a library
story.body: This is the work that continues after a DAM or vocabulary is stood up: who owns a file, what it can be used for, when it comes back for review.

experience.json.title: Content platforms & architecture
experience.json.subtitle: CMS models, authoring, audits
experience.json.summary: Reusable models, the forms editors type into, and the inventory that shows what to keep.

story.label: Practice
story.title: Fitting the platform to the task
story.body: If the model and the form don’t match how people publish, they work around both. These projects are about that fit: records, references and checks at the point of entry.

experience.json.title: Editorial delivery & enablement
experience.json.subtitle: Workflow, release, handover
experience.json.summary: Getting work from request to live, then leaving the next owner able to run it without asking me.

story.label: Practice
story.title: From request to live, then handover
story.body: A workflow is only useful if it names an owner and a publish check. Handover is the same problem later: tasks, sources of truth, and who keeps the guidance current.

mixes.json.title: After hours
mixes.json.subtitle: Deep house
mixes.json.summary: Late-night deep house. Starts warm and open, then tightens once the floor is in.

story.label: Listening notes
story.title: When the room is already moving
story.body: This is the stretch after people have arrived. Spacious at the front so it does not feel like a restart, then a more focused groove once the floor has a centre. File goes on when I have one to share.

mixes.json.title: Open air
mixes.json.subtitle: House
mixes.json.summary: Daytime house selection for outdoors and afternoons. Unhurried, so the rhythm takes its time.

story.label: Listening notes
story.title: Outdoors and afternoons
story.body: Outdoor or afternoon, you can’t pack the density you would at 1am. This selection stays open: house that can sit under conversation and still hold a floor if people want one.

mixes.json.title: Night shift
mixes.json.subtitle: Electronic
mixes.json.summary: Peak-hour electronic. Tighter pulse, a slow climb, less space between the hits.

story.label: Listening notes
story.title: The driving stretch
story.body: The kick is closer, the changes are smaller, and the energy is meant to hold rather than reset. I wouldn’t open a night with it.

mixes.json.title: Soft focus
mixes.json.subtitle: Downtempo
mixes.json.summary: A listening selection. Texture, space, and a quieter pace than the dancefloor records.

story.label: Listening notes
story.title: For bars and closing
story.body: For a bar, the end of a night, or a room that wants records more than a set. The pace drops and the detail comes forward. It’s still a selection, not a playlist.

mixes.json.title: First light
mixes.json.subtitle: Ambient
mixes.json.summary: A slow open: sustained tones, long transitions, space between anything that resembles a beat.

story.label: Listening notes
story.title: The first half hour
story.body: Doors, early rooms, or the first half hour when you don’t want to force a groove. Tones hold the space, and the next selection can go anywhere from here.
